pairs.subject: self-describing-model-packages
pairs.evidence: packages/voice-stt/src/providers/whisper-cpp.ts:133 The package does not create, describe or export a model package: it finds third-party whisper.cpp GGML files by their upstream ggml-*.bin filename and passes them to the external whisper-cli binary. A search of packages/voice-stt for $schema, schema, schema_version, format_version, logits and symbolic found no hits, so this context has no package metadata, schema, shape rule or export for the techniques to govern.

techniques.evidence: packages/voice-stt/src/providers/whisper-cpp.ts:115 Only consumes the upstream GGML naming convention; the package defines no layout of its own.
packages/voice-stt/src/providers/whisper-cpp.ts:40 The input is a 16 kHz WAV file handed to a CLI, not a tensor shape family this package declares or proves.
packages/voice-stt/src/providers/whisper-cpp.ts:204 The output is whisper-cli's JSON transcript; the package declares no raw or derived network outputs.
packages/voice-stt/package.json:3 The only version is the npm library's own; no model package records the framework or engine versions it was built on.

It creates no package, schema or export of its own. A search of packages/voice-tts for $schema, schema, schema_version, format_version, logits and symbolic found no hits.

techniques.evidence: packages/voice-tts/src/providers/kokoro.ts:52 Uses the fixed upstream sherpa-onnx Kokoro layout; the layout belongs to upstream, not to this package.
packages/voice-tts/src/providers/piper.ts:52 Reads one field from upstream Piper metadata whose format it does not own; it has no schema of its own to name.
packages/voice-tts/src/providers/piper.ts:98 The output is the WAV file the piper CLI writes; no network output is declared here.
packages/voice-tts/package.json:3 The only version is the npm library's own; no built-on framework or engine versions are recorded for any model.

pairs.registryProposal: The golden path's use_when lists 'validating a third-party model package before running it', but all six techniques are written from the author's side. A consumer-side rule (for example, check the upstream package's own metadata contract instead of a size proxy or a single cast field) would make thin adapter consumers like these judgeable rather than not-applicable.
